scope.activation: optional host-owned startup argument after package directory

proof_state.unbound: no signed claim and no tensor
proof_state.host_signature_verified: trusted issuer signature binds current plan, full manifest SHA-256, logical port, source, subject, metadata, nonce and exact f32 bytes
proof_state.stale_or_unbound: signed claim no longer describes the current manifest or bound port
proof_state.replay: duplicate issuer nonce or non-increasing revision is rejected before bind; 50000 accepted claims maximum per process or durable ledger and then fail closed
proof_state.authority: Node host transport gate only; Burn remains numerical reference authority

canonical_claim.encoding: UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify in canonicalInputClaim insertion order
canonical_claim.signature: Ed25519 detached signature encoded as canonical base64
canonical_claim.value_sha256: SHA-256 of ordered little-endian IEEE-754 f32 values submitted to WasmTensor

valid_transitions: host loads trusted issuer public keys and explicit allowed subjects before accepting JSON Lines
create snapshots multi-input plan and logical manifest
bind verifies exact current signed claim, subject, nonce and increasing revision before mutating bundle
run and verify require signed coverage for every runtime port and repeat the existing WASM preflight
clear removes a slot's proof while keeping nonce and revision replay history for the process
manifest change invalidates old signatures until inputs are cleared and signed again
limits: The trust policy file and producer private keys must be controlled outside the JSON Lines caller.
Without a host ledger, replay history lasts for the runner process; the optional host-owned file ledger preserves it across restarts.
When the 50000-claim process replay window is full, new binds fail closed rather than evicting nonce history.
A direct caller of the exported WASM API can bypass this Node host gate.
An issuer signature authenticates that issuer's claim; it does not establish the truth of observations or authorize agent decisions.
FNV fingerprints remain diagnostic correlation only; the signed claim binds full manifest SHA-256 and plan bytes.
